title: Decision, Start-Date and Notification Timetable for Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
For every tier of **Hardship and Protective Holds**, the timetable below fixes how quickly a request is decided, which date an approved hold starts from, how quickly the decision letter goes out, and whether — and how quickly — the placing client is told of an approval.

## Timetable

| Tier | Decision time (business days) | Hold starts from | Decision letter time (business days) | Client told of approval | Client notification time (business days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30-Day Hardship Pause | 1 | Decision date | 1 | No | 0 |
| Documented Hardship Hold | 5 | Decision date | 2 | No | 0 |
| Disaster Relief Hold | 3 | Decision date | 2 | No | 0 |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | 5 | Request date | 2 | Yes | 2 |
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | 10 | Decision date | 3 | No | 0 |
| Military Service Hold | 3 | Request date | 2 | Yes | 2 |

## What each column means

- **Decision time** — the business days after complete documentation (or after the request, where none is needed) within which the request is decided.
- **Hold starts from** — which date the hold starts from: the decision date or the request date.
- **Decision letter time** — the business days after the decision within which the approval or denial letter is sent.
- **Client told of approval** — whether the client is notified when the hold is approved.
- **Client notification time** — the business days after approval within which the client is notified; 0 where no notification is required.

## Points of reading

- Two tiers start from the request date: the Financial Assistance Review Hold and the Military Service Hold. An approved hold of either tier therefore begins on the date the request was received, whichever day the approval is given. Every other tier starts on its decision date.
- The same two tiers are the only ones whose approval is notified to the client, in each case within 2 business days.
- The 30-Day Hardship Pause needs no documentation, so its decision time of 1 business day runs from the request itself.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Military Service Hold request is received on a Monday and approved on the Wednesday of the same week. Because the tier starts from the request date, the first day of the hold is the Monday. A Documented Hardship Hold approved on that same Wednesday would instead start on the Wednesday, its decision date.
